newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP Steel plays down Indonesian reports.
newsitem.headline: BHP Steel plays down Indonesian reports.

text.p: BHP Steel chief executive Ron McNeilly said on Tuesday that BHP's potential interest in Indonesia's PT Krakatau Steel had been overstated in recent Indonesian newspaper reports.

"I think the report in the newspaper that appeared in Jakarta yesterday significantly overstated the situation and we will certainly be making it very clear to the (Australian) Prime Minister just what the circumstances are," McNeilly said.
"There shouldn't be too much read into the article at this time," he told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.

The Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported that BHP Steel, a division of The Broken Hill Propritary Co Ltd, planned to take a 25 percent stake in the Indonesian government-owned PT Krakatau in a private placement before it was floated later in 1997.

The reports coincide with a visit by Australian Prime Minister John Howard to the city of Newcastle, north of Sydney, later this week. BHP plans to end steelmaking at Newcastle in two years time with the loss of 2,500 jobs.
"No way are we looking at steelmaking anywhere overseas in lieu of steelmaking in Australia," McNeilly said.
"It is just not on the agenda at all," he said. However, he said downstream investments in the Asia/Pacific region were always under investigation.
BHP officials said earlier in response to the Indonesian reports that the company had held talks with PT Krakatau but no final investment decisions had been made.
